root_causes.evidence: Gateway was up=false and not_answering with no release or config change; a restart restored it to baseline p95 and rps.
The scheduler changed max_transfer_minor from 1000000 to 1, an unworkable limit, just before payments rejects rose to 10-41%; reverting it brought rejects back to 0.

actions.reason: Gateway is not answering (process down) and payments had max_transfer_minor set to 1, an unworkable limit; restart gateway first.
Now revert the payments transfer limit change to 1 minor unit, which blocks nearly all payments.
actions.detail: payments max_transfer_minor restored from 1 to 1000000 (changed earlier by scheduler)

sbar.situation: The bank system has recovered and is running normally. A probe passes end to end and all metrics are at baseline, confirmed clean on two checks in a row, the last at 39 seconds.
sbar.background: The gateway process went down with no release or config change. Separately, the scheduler changed the payments setting max_transfer_minor from 1000000 to 1, and payments rejects then rose to 10-41%.
sbar.assessment: Two root causes were found: the gateway process was down (confidence 0.9), and the payments max_transfer_minor setting was bad (confidence 0.95). The incident commander restarted the gateway itself, which restored baseline p95 and rps. It also reverted max_transfer_minor to 1000000 itself, which brought payments rejects back to 0.
sbar.recommendation: Find out why the scheduler set max_transfer_minor to 1 and stop it happening again. Ask the owning team why ops-maintenance and the pipeline restarted screening-standby three times, though it is healthy on release 4.1. Operations should review the payments rejected while rejects ran at 10-41%.
